sources.facts: CurrentDOC operator describes an1870s tunnel commissioned by JohnCargill, chipped through solid sandstone with picks/shovels. Stepped short tunnel has rough rock walls/low ceiling/no handrail/no artificial light. Distinct natural rock arch is a separate headland feature.

Operator reports track reopening14November2025 after2024 storm slips, with track stabilization/drainage/resurfacing. No unsupported claim that historic tunnel was demolished; do not copy repaired whole-walk infrastructure from old photographs.

Published Qualla story says72 concrete interior steps installed1983. Treat as story-sourced census, not measured geometry; do not confuse coastal cliff height or nearby approach-step counts with passage length.

Individually inspected exact native3600x1600 Ingolfson creator-PD original montage already published as Qualla hero. Shows upper rough-hewn sandstone entrance, straight ascending narrow barrel-profile stair tunnel/daylight at far portal, and beach/cliff context. Native transferred source/explicit original PD-self. Use actual montage as reference, no claim it is one continuous photographic perspective. No distant sea stacks/waves/cliff landscape copied into a building asset.

Shows surrounding descending access path/coastal bluff and natural sea arch at distance; terrain/context only. Natural arch is distinct from the human-carved tunnel and is excluded from this structure model.
